title: Effects of Marathon Running on Aerobic Fitness and Performance in Recreational Runners One Week after a Race
authors: Takayama F, Aoyagi A, Shimazu W, Nabekura Y
population: 11 recreational marathon runners (6 men, 5 women), finish time 3 h 36 min 20 s +/- 41 min 34 s
findings: Treadmill test before and 7 days after the race: VO2max change -1.2 ml/kg/min (possibly trivial).
Velocity at anaerobic threshold -0.2 km/h and peak velocity -0.3 km/h (both likely trivial); %VO2max at AT -0.5% and running economy +0.2 ml/kg/km (both unclear).
Perceived muscle soreness increased until 3 days after the race, with no clear differences from pre-race values 4 to 7 days after.
Authors conclude that physiological capacity associated with marathon running performance is recovered within 7 days after a marathon.
limitations: n = 11, one race, recreational runners; magnitude-based inference with unclear effects for economy and threshold %VO2max; treadmill test, not a race effort.
implications: Supports that in recreational marathoners aerobic determinants are largely intact at day 7, so a hold plus return that regains normal training within roughly 1 to 2 weeks is plausible for a marathon.
Soreness had no clear difference from pre-race by day 4 in this sample, so a soreness check-in is a reasonable gate for the marathon easy-running window (day 2 to 6), consistent with the RCT above.
Not applicable to ultras, where Hoffman shows soreness clears before speed does.

verification.notes: Crossref gives authors Takayama, Aoyagi, Shimazu, Nabekura; the record's 'Takahashi K' was wrong and is corrected. Abstract re-read (PMID 29138757); all numbers and the 7-day conclusion match.
